label: input j late in an original sequence that starts r, b
explanation: Very sparse: active on only 21 of 1M sequences (12 steps in dev). Every activation is in the original phase, on input j (11 of 12, about 98% of mass; 1 weak q right after a j), at t=4-7, in sequences whose first token is r. Most also have b as the third original token, and b usually repeats (r q b b p j is the top example). Magnitude is highest when j comes at t=5 after r q b b. It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, and never on j in sequences that do not start with r. Precision is low even for the tightest predicate (r ... j only: P=0.004; with orig(2)==b and t>=4: P=0.2, R=0.75 on dev), so this reads as a narrow memorized-context feature with too few examples to characterize reliably.
